answer: The system clusters submissions into pools based on timing, funding, and wording patterns. If two identities share a signature kernel above 80% in a lagoon of recent submissions, the newer one is delayed by 180 seconds. Attackers must queue each fake identity separately, incurring a per-head cost of linear time delays. A harbor of thresholds ensures that no bulk submission flooding is possible, as each identity must wait its own turn under a prism of scrutiny.
